subject: Intermittent egress failures — connmark/stateful rollback?
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-payments.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: noc@acme-payments.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent egress failures from private deployment (starts 07:45 PT)

Dylan —

We're seeing intermittent egress failures from our private deployment in us-west-2 starting ~07:45 PT this morning. Symptoms: short (~30s) blackouts to external payment partners (TCP RSTs, flows drop), then traffic returns without a clear config change on our side.

We confirmed via our NOC that:
- issue appears across two subnets behind the Redwood private connector
- no obvious host-level restarts; kernel logs show large conntrack churn around 07:44–07:48
- we've attached a pcap from one affected host and our iptables-save from before/after the window

Can someone from Redwood take a look? This impacts a small subset of payments and we need an ETA.

Attachments: p4-tcpdump-09-30.pcap (tcpdump), iptables-save-before-after.txt

Thanks,
Alice
Senior SRE, Acme Payments
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-payments.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from private deployment (starts 07:45 PT)

Thanks for the quick ping and attachments, Alice. We're looking into this now. High-level plan:

1) I'll triage the pcap and conntrack churn; Jonás, can you validate NAT gateway/connmark rules and any recent route updates?
2) Irene, please scope whether our private connector pushed any stateful rollback or iptables rule that could cause connmark drops.
3) We'll share findings in 30 min and propose a mitigation (temporary rule soften or session timeout bump) if needed.

A few quick asks to narrow scope:
- Can you confirm the affected hosts' AMI/kernel version? (we suspect conntrack load sensitivity)
- Sample tcpdump has SYN+RST pairs; do you have a server-side application log showing connection close reason?

Alice — we'll keep you posted. If possible, leave the capture running for 10 more minutes.

--
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Private Deployments 
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from private deployment (starts 07:45 PT)

Quick update from infra side after initial checks:

- No route table changes in the last 24h in the customer's VPC.
- NAT gateway metrics look normal but conntrack entries spiked ~07:44; simultaneous churn across two NAT instances.
- I pulled iptables-save snapshots Alice attached; I see a connmark-based mangle rule we rolled out as part of "connmark session affinity" last week (rule chain: PREROUTING -t mangle -j CONNMARK --set-mark 0x400).

Hypothesis: the connmark mangle interacts poorly with our stateful offload on EdgeCloud's user-plane (EdgeCloud recently rolled a kernel patch for connmark offload). Under high churn, the connmark state is partially lost and connections receive RSTs when translation fails.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Rollback the connmark mangle on the affected NAT instances (fast, should stop churn-induced RSTs).
- Alternatively, increase conntrack hash size/timeouts to tolerate bursts (safer but slower).

I recommend rollback on the two NAT instances in us-west-2 during a 5-min maintenance window. I'll prepare the commands and a runbook.

Jonas
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-payments.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: noc@acme-payments.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from private deployment (starts 07:45 PT)

Thanks Jonas — that matches what our kernel team suspected (EdgeCloud kernel change may surface). We can approve a short rollback window. Please note: any change to NAT/path must be communicated to our ops channel before execution.

We've attached an additional pcap and a screenshot of our security group snapshot around the event (sg-snapshot-before.png). From our side nothing looks like it intentionally rejects traffic; it appears to be translation/state.

Please proceed with rollback and ping when done.

Alice
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-payments.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, EdgeCloud Support <support@edgecloud.io>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from private deployment (starts 07:45 PT)

Final post-mortem summary: action completed and validation OK.

What we did:
- 2026-09-30 09:20 PT: Rolled back the connmark mangle rule on the two affected NAT instances in us-west-2 (commands in attached iptables-save-before-after.txt).
- 2026-09-30 09:23 PT: Increased conntrack max_entries from 262144 -> 524288 and bumped tcp timeout to reduce churn risk.
- 2026-09-30 09:30 PT: Monitored for 60 minutes; no further RST bursts observed and pcap sampling showed normal SYN->SYN/ACK flows.

Root cause:
- Interaction between our connmark-based session affinity mangle and a recent EdgeCloud kernel connmark offload patch caused transient loss of connmark state under bursty connection churn. That led to failed NAT translations and TCP resets.

Follow-ups and mitigations:
- We'll coordinate with EdgeCloud to test the connmark offload patch against our connmark ruleset in a staging environment.
- Implement a deploy-time check that flags connmark/conntrack-sensitive rules when kernel offload flags are present.
- Add a dashboard alert for sudden conntrack churn (>50% baseline) to auto-escalate earlier.

Attachments: iptables-save-before-after.txt (commands + before/after), p4-tcpdump-09-30.pcap (sample), sg-snapshot-before.png

Thanks for the quick coordination, Alice. Let us know if you see anything else from Acme's side. Jonas and Irene — please open the INF ticket and include the EdgeCloud contact for validation.

--
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
